ours.name: West Ridge / Southwest Face
ours.approach: From SR 20 near Newhalem, park at the Goodell Creek Group Campground (~600 ft) just east of Goodell Creek. The climbers' path starts behind a large boulder at the back of the campground and follows the old Goodell Creek roadbed upvalley for roughly 3.5-4 miles of gentle but brushy going (expect deadfall and a handful of washouts - this is an unmaintained boot path, not a maintained trail); two creek crossings low on the path can run high and fast on hot afternoons from snowmelt. An obvious cairn near 1,700 ft marks where the route leaves the roadbed and climbs steeply up a timbered spur ridge south of Terror Creek, passing about 3,200 ft on the way up. fktText: Description West McMillan Spire, Southern Pickets, North Cascades, Washington – Standard Route via Goodell Creek The Notch Trailhead : Goodell Creek Trailhead, accessed via SR-20 to Newhalem, then Goodell Creek Road (just east of Goodell Campground) to the Upper Goodell Creek Group Camp. The unmarked trail starts near a large boulder behind the campground. No permit required for a single-push day trip; a North Cascades National Park backcountry permit is required for overnight camping in Terror Basin. Distance/Gain : Approximately 20 miles round trip with over 10,000 ft of elevation gain, car-to-car. Route : From the trailhead, the climbers' path follows Goodell Creek for ~4 miles before climbing steeply to about 3,200 ft where it levels onto a forested ridge. The trail continues through heather benches and blueberry fields to treeline, then ascends to a notch in the ridge, then descending a steep, loose scramble down the far side into Terror Basin. From the basin, traverse north toward the glacial lake at the base of the peak, following cairns and a faint boot path. Ascend snow and rock toward the Terror Glacier and the base of West McMillan's west ridge. A steep gully (snow or loose scree, depending on the time of year) leads up to the ridge crest, followed by Class 3 rock and ledge systems to the summit. ours.name: Fish & Whistle
ours.approach: Same approach as True Grit and Ragged Edge: Sunrise Mine Trail #707 from the Sunrise Mine Trailhead, through Wirtz Basin and Headlee Pass (~4,720 ft, 2.7 mi, loose rock/rockfall in the narrow couloir), down to Vesper Creek and up a short rise to Vesper Lake (Lake Elan, ~4,950 ft, ~3.5 mi/~2,700 ft gain — last water), then off-trail up the talus ridge to the Vesper-Wolf col and across the exposed heather ledge system at ~5,800 ft (slick when wet, holds snow into mid-to-late summer — ice axe useful early season). ours.descent: Fish & Whistle climbs the same upper north-face headwall as True Grit and finishes in the same general area near the top of the face/summit ridge, so the standard exit is almost certainly the same walk-off used for True Grit and Ragged Edge: scramble down the southeast side (a seasonal snow slope early on, open slabs/talus by late summer) back to the Vesper-Wolf saddle, then down to Vesper Lake an

fktText: Description A classic Cascades scramble with big payoff for relatively little technical skill required. From the Sunrise Mine Trail, cross Vesper Creek instead of heading toward Vesper Lake. A bootpath climbs steeply through heather, cedar, and rocky slopes before breaking onto granite slabs. From here, it’s straightforward off-trail scrambling: mostly low-angle rock, with light hands-on moves and easy routefinding. Stay on the central rib to avoid gullies (left) or exposure (right). The airy summit delivers commanding views of Del Campo, Gothic, Sperry, Big Four, and the Vesper Glacier dropping to Copper Lake. ours.name: East Ledges
ours.approach: Start at the Boston Basin trailhead off the Cascade River Road. A steep climbers' trail with several creek crossings (Boston Creek can run high on warm afternoons) climbs to the camps in Boston Basin; overnight stays there need a park backcountry permit. From the upper basin, head north toward Forbidden's South Face and climb the snow slopes and loose gully below and right of it to the East Ridge saddle just northwest of the Solitary Gendarme, about 8,300–8,400 ft. Allow about 4 hours from the trailhead to the saddle, or about 2 hours from the basin camps. Axe and crampons are usually needed for this snow; late in the season they can be left at the saddle.
ours.descent: The usual descent is the ascent line reversed. From a horn near the summit, make the first of five single-rope rappels (roughly 400 ft total) down the northeast side to a series of ledges, then follow the ledges east - mostly 3rd class with short 4th-class moves at rib crossings - across roughly five rock ribs before a short gully leads back up to the East Ridge crest near the solitary gendarme. fktText: Description The west ridge of Forbidden peak is one of the 50 american classics and sits in the heart of the North Cascades of Washington state. It challenges hikers and runners to gain the steep basin to reach the summit. The route starts at the boston basin trailhead at 3,223 ft and finishes at 8,783 ft returning to the car for a 8mi loop and 5,603 ft of vert packing in a solid day of mixed skills. The route starts at the Boston Basin trailhead with light running and steep trails to Boston Basin high camp at about 6,500 ft. After traversing the high alpine meadows you gain the couloir to the left edge of the South Face of Forbidden Peak. This is where the climbing starts to the true summit. You return by rappelling down the north face to and scrambling back to the notch where you started climbing. A few more repels take you back to the slab rock where you run back the way you came. This route is the perfect combo of trail running, alpine hiking, scrambling and a little climbing. This route is a favorite for many in the western states attracting 100's of people regularly. ours.name: East Ridge Direct
ours.approach: Same trailhead and Boston Basin climbers' trail as the West Ridge (old Diamond Mine roadbed for ~1 mile, then a steep climbers' path with several creek crossings to treeline around 5,300 ft, then talus/heather to the usual high camp at 6,300–6,600 ft, roughly 4–5 miles / 3–4 hours from the car). From camp, rather than crossing toward the south-face couloir, traverse climber's-left/east around the basin and gain the ridges and gullies flanking the glacier on Forbidden's east side (sometimes loosely called the 'Unnamed Glacier'). ours.name: North Ridge
ours.approach: North-northeast via glacier traversals. From Boston Basin parking, hike to Boston Basin high camp (~6400 ft). Traverse moraine and west edge of Quien Sabe Glacier to 7,500 ft. Climb to Sharkfin Col (7,720 ft).
ours.descent: The North Ridge finishes on the summit, and the way off is the West Ridge. Downclimb and rappel the West Ridge to the notch (one rope is enough for the rappels, and several anchors exist, so the mix is a matter of choice), then downclimb or rappel the snow couloir below the notch into Boston Basin; the Cat Scratch Gully to the climber's left is a rappel alternative. ours.name: Northeast Face
ours.approach: From Boston Basin Trailhead, hike ~3-4 mi via old mine road then a climbers' path (4 stream crossings) to high camp near 6,400 ft (3-4 hrs). Continue along the moraine and west edge of the Quien Sabe Glacier to Sharkfin Col (~7,720 ft) via ~10 ft of 5.7 rock and a Class 3 gully. Rappel into the bergschrund on the far side and climb a short ice wall to gain the Boston Glacier, then traverse west across the Boston Glacier to the base of the Northeast Face below a prominent ice patch.
ours.descent: Do not reverse the Northeast Face. Most parties descend by the West Ridge, as below; the East Ledges off the northeast side are the faster but looser, harder-to-follow alternative. ours.name: Northwest Face
ours.approach: From Boston Basin Trailhead, hike ~3-4 mi via old mine road then a climbers' path (4 stream crossings) to high camp near 6,400 ft (3-4 hrs), often continuing to a bench at ~7,500 ft beside the Quien Sabe Glacier below Sharkfin Tower. Ascend the west side of the Quien Sabe Glacier to a notch above Sharkfin Col, rappel onto the Boston Glacier below the bergschrund, traverse the heavily crevassed Boston Glacier, then continue around to the north arm of the Forbidden Glacier. Climb ~900 ft of 30-40+ degree snow/ice to reach the base of the technical rock (5.6 knife-edge ridge leading into the 5.8 crux). Most parties treat this as a 3-day trip.
ours.descent: Do not reverse the Northwest Face; descend by the standard West Ridge. From the true summit, downclimb back past the false summit to the crux tower, then work down the West Ridge crest with exposed 3rd/4th-class downclimbing and about 3 rappels off slung horns and blocks, back to the West Ridge notch. ours.name: West Ridge
ours.approach: From the Boston Basin trailhead off Cascade River Road, follow the unsigned but well-beaten Boston Basin climbers' path. It starts by following the old Diamond Mine roadbed for about 1 mile, then splits off the roadbed to climb steeply and directly through forest. The trail crosses four seasonal creeks/streams (reliable water) as it switchbacks up through increasingly open timber, breaking out above treeline around 5,300 ft. Above treeline it continues into the broad boulder-and-heather Boston Basin cirque, past the usual high-camp sites around 6,300–6,600 ft (roughly 4–5 miles and 3–4 hours from the car, ringed by Sahale, Sharkfin Tower, and Mt. ours.name: Southwest Route
ours.approach: From the Upper Goodell Creek Group Campground trailhead (end of the short Goodell Creek Road spur off the North Cascades Highway near Newhalem, ~600 ft), follow the unmaintained but well-trodden Goodell Creek climbers' trail, which runs along an old overgrown logging road bed paralleling Goodell Creek. The first roughly 4.5 miles are comparatively mellow, mostly forested walking to the old 'spar tree,' where a boot path cut by Seattle Mountaineers work parties continues on. ours.descent: There is no walk-off: descend by downclimbing and rappelling the Southwest Arête back toward camp. The in-place rap stations are old fixed and natural anchors (slings around horns and blocks, older bolts or pitons) rather than fresh bolted chains. fktText: Description Route submitted by Ryan Stoddard : This route is in the Sawtooth sub-range of WA's Cascades. The only requirements are to start and end at Crater Creek TH and summit the five top 100 "Bulger" list peaks along the way: Switchback, Bigelow, Martin, Raven Ridge, Hoodoo. Note that the True summit of Raven Ridge is a little east of the ridge line (this one: https://peakbagger.com/peak.aspx?pid=28897 ) not Libby Peak. ours.name: Tribute to Richard
ours.approach: Drive to the Crater Creek Trailhead (4,750 ft, 48.2205 / -120.26801). From Twisp take SR 20 south 2 miles to the SR 153 junction, then SR 153 south about 12 miles to County Road 1029 and on to CR 1034 (Gold Creek Road). CR 1034 becomes Forest Road 4340 after roughly 5 miles; continue about 1.6 miles further on FR 4340, then turn onto FR 4340-300 (Crater Creek Road) and follow it 4.6 miles to the trailhead. An alternate description of the same drive starts from Carlton: south on SR 153 for 3.5 miles, right on Gold Creek Loop Road 1.6 miles, right on Gold Creek Road 5.0 miles (becomes FR 4340), 1.6 miles more, then left on FR 4340-300 for 4.4 miles. ours.name: Torment-Forbidden Traverse
ours.approach: From the Boston Basin trailhead pullout on Cascade River Road (~3,300 ft, opposite Johannesburg Mountain, roughly mile 22-23), follow the old abandoned mining road for about 0.75 mile to the historic mine site. From there an unmaintained but well-beaten climbers' path takes over, switchbacking steeply up through forest with four creek/stream crossings to treeline around 5,300 ft. Above the trees the path eases across heather benches and talus into Boston Basin proper; low camp sits around 5,300-5,500 ft and high camp around 6,400 ft (total roughly 2.5-3 miles and 3,000-3,300 ft gain from car to high camp, 2.5-4 hours). ours.descent: The traverse finishes by descending Forbidden Peak, not Torment, so 'descent' here means the way off Forbidden's summit back to Boston Basin.
